gen-eater-fs-erode: Eater looks menacing, all thin strokes and spaced-out letters. Erode, a serif, answers with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight and a tall middle band, which gives the dark heading a dignified, editorial footing.
gen-eater-fs-trench-slab: Dark and jagged up top, then steadier below. Trench Slab, a serif, keeps its capitals barely above the x-height, and a long stretch of it reads dense, refined and dignified.
gen-eater-gf-domine: Refined and dignified, Domine keeps its ascenders compact over tall lowercase, with a breathing space inside every curve. Eater is the one for menace; Domine is the one for steady text.
gen-eater-gf-esteban: Classic in manner, Esteban is a text serif with thin parts barely slimmer than its stems. Over a longer passage its oversized lowercase and open e keep the reading easy and unhurried, far from Eater's snarl.
gen-eater-gf-faustina: Faustina, a text serif, has an open-jawed c and capitals only slightly taller than its lowercase, so it reads with quiet authority. A longer passage would feel steady and classic.
gen-eater-gf-halant: Spiky and a little sinister, Eater leads with wide gaps between its letters. And Halant, a classic serif, brings a towering x-height and outward-pointing terminals, so give that body size some room.
gen-eater-gf-hedvig-letters-serif: Authoritative from the first line, Eater is all aggression and spaced-out strokes. But Hedvig Letters Serif, a text serif, has sturdy lowercase, so making the body large would make it feel heavy-handed.
gen-eater-gf-lisu-bosa: Eater snarls, jagged and loose. Lisu Bosa, a text serif, does the opposite job: its tall lowercase makes words look sturdy, and its counters spill into the space around them, which is what the heading cannot do.
gen-eater-gf-marcellus-sc: Eater bites hard, thin strokes and wide gaps everywhere. Its menace is the heading's best trick, while Marcellus SC, a classic serif, does its best work with pulled-back terminals and a gentle, literary stroke modulation.
gen-eater-gf-montagu-slab: Eater brings dark, aggressive spacing and thin strokes to the heading, with short ascenders over its body height. Montagu Slab, a classic serif, handles the reading, with robust downstrokes and slender turns.
